'''Sundararaman Ramanan''' (born 20 July 1937) is an Indian [[mathematician]] who works in the area of [[algebraic geometry]], [[moduli space]]s and [[Lie group]]s. He is one of India's leading mathematicians and recognised as an expert in algebraic geometry, especially in the area of moduli problems. He has also worked in differential geometry: his joint paper with MS Narasimhan on universal connections has been influential. It enabled SS Chern and B Simons to introduce what is known as the Chern-Simons invariant, which has proved useful in theoretical physics.<ref>[http://www.mat.csic.es/webpages/moduli2008/ramanan/ A conference in honour of S Ramanan] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080926120229/http://www.mat.csic.es/webpages/moduli2008/ramanan/ |date=26 September 2008}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
He is an alumnus of the [[Ramakrishna Mission School]] in Chennai and the [[Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College|Vivekananda College]] in Chennai, where he completed a BA Honours in mathematics.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}} He completed his PhD at the [[TIFR|Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], under the direction of [[Mudumbai Seshachalu Narasimhan|MS Narasimhan]]. He did his post-doctoral studies at the [[University of Oxford]], [[Harvard University]] and [[ETH Zurich]].{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

He later pursued a career at TIFR. He picked up the methods of modern differential geometry from the French mathematician [[Jean-Louis Koszul]],<ref>Koszul, J.-L. Lectures on fibre bundles and differential geometry. With notes by S Ramanan. Reprint of the 1965 edition. Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Lectures on Mathematics and Physics, 20. Published for the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Bombay; by Springer-Verlag, Berlin, 1986. Viii+127 pp. {{ISBN|3-540-12876-X}}</ref> and later successfully applied it for his research centred on algebraic geometry. He has also made contributions to the topics of [[Abelian variety]] and [[vector bundles]].

== Collaborations and influences ==
He collaborated with [[Raoul Bott]], who was at [[Harvard University]]. He has been a visiting professor at Harvard University, [[University of California at Berkeley]], the Institute of Advanced Study in [[Princeton University|Princeton]], [[UCLA]], [[University of Oxford]], [[Cambridge University]], the Max Planck Institute and [[University of Paris]].{{citation needed|date=March 2019}} In 1978, he gave one of the invited talks at the International Congress of Mathematicians in [[Helsinki]]. In 1999, he spoke about some aspects of the work of [[André Weil]] on the occasion of his being awarded the Inamouri Prize.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

Ramanan discovered and encouraged [[Vijay Kumar Patodi]], who proved part of the [[Atiyah-Singer index theorem]], Patodi did his PhD under the combined direction of Narasimhan and Ramanan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Mathematicians/Patodi.html |title=Patodi biography |publisher=History.mcs.st-and.ac.uk |access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref> Ramanan was [[M S Raghunathan|MS Raghunathan's]] senior colleague and influenced him considerably.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~dani/msrfr.pdf|title=S. G. Dani on MS Raghunathan|access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref>

Ramanan wrote the book ''Moduli of Abelian Varieties'' with Allan Adler, published by Springer-Verlag, and a graduate-level book on algebraic geometry called ''Global Calculus'', published by the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/bookstore?arg9=S._Ramanan&f=G&fn=105&p=0&pg1=CN&r=1&s1=Ramanan_S |title=AMS page on the book titled Global Calculus |publisher=Ams.org |access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref> He continues his contributions via teaching and mentoring at the [[Chennai Mathematical Institute]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cmi.ac.in/people/fac-profile.php?id=sramanan|title=Chennai Mathematical Institute faculty page|publisher=Cmi.ac.in|access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref> where he is an adjunct professor, and at the [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai]].

== Awards ==
Ramanan received the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], India's highest science prize,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/MATHEMATICAL_SCIENCES.htm|title=List of Bhatnagar award recipients in mathematical sciences|publisher=Csir.res.in|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120218182837/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/MATHEMATICAL_SCIENCES.htm|archive-date=18 February 2012|access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref> in 1979; the [[TWAS Prize]] for Mathematics in 2001<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web|url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards|title=Prizes and Awards|date=2016|publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and the Ramanujan Medal in 2008.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

== Personal life ==
He is married to Anuradha Ramanan, a translator and former librarian. They have two daughters, Sumana Ramanan, a journalist, and [[Kavita Ramanan]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.cmu.edu/users/kramanan/ |title=Kavita Ramanan |publisher=Math.cmu.edu |access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref> a noted mathematician who is a professor of applied mathematics at [[Brown University]] in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].
